In mathematics, the '''Taniyama group''' is a [[Group (mathematics)|group]] that is an [[Group extension|extension]] of the [[absolute Galois group]] of the [[Rational number|rationals]] by the [[Serre group]]. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Langlands|authorlink=Robert Langlands|year=1977}}<ref>{{citation |last=Langlands |first=R. P. |title=Automorphic forms, representations and L-functions |volume=33 |pages=205–246 |year=1977 |series=Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. |chapter=Automorphic representations, Shimura varieties, and motives. Ein Märchen |isbn=0-8218-1437-0 |mr=0546619 |authorlink=Robert Langlands}}</ref> using an observation by [[Deligne]], and named after [[Yutaka Taniyama]]. It was intended to be the [[group scheme]] whose representations correspond to the (hypothetical) [[Complex multiplication|CM]] [[Motive (algebraic geometry)|motives]] over the field '''Q''' of rational numbers.
